text:
maria: Thinking out loud — for the automatic fallback UX I'm leaning toward a 'soft switchover' slider rather than a binary toggle. gives us a visible grace window and backoff curve. thoughts?

leon: +1 for a slider. users ask about "how long before we cut" all the time. a default of 250ms feels reasonable.

anya: Agree on slider. We should show an estimated cost/latency tradeoff next to it (tiny chart). helps PMs justify changes.

vik: Important: distinguish between 'soft switchover' (route a % of requests) and 'grace padding' (delay before fallback triggers). both useful.

maria: Yeah — UX should expose two knobs: 1) staging window (ms) 2) ramp percentage. staging window is the padding, ramp is gradual shift.

leon: What about error signatures? e.g., only trigger fallback for 5xx vs model-specific semantic failures. need a dropdown to pick triggers.

maria: +1 on trigger selector. propose: 
- HTTP errors (5xx, 429)
- Model runtime errors (OOM, kernel)
- Quality regressions (eval set alerts)

anya: We should also add a lightweight "preview" simulation button that replays recent traffic and shows how many requests would have hit fallback with current settings.

maria: mock config snippet for the UX preview:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  mode: soft_swap
  staging_padding_ms: 300
  ramp_pct: 20
  triggers: [5xx, oom, quality_regression]
```

sam: If we expose staging_padding_ms, we need a help tooltip: "padding delays the decision so short transient spikes don't flip routes." short copy.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: recent spike at 2025-09-03T14:22:18Z with 5xx burst, median latency +120ms.

vik: Audit visibility: each automatic switchover should write an immutable breadcrumb entry with config snapshot + sample IDs of affected requests. Console needs a small timeline row for that.

leon: Also capture reverted actions: who changed the slider and when, and a one-click rollback to previous policy.

maria: UX mock idea: show three small states inline — idle / soft-swapping (with % and padding) / fully-fallback. color-coded, with keyboard accessible controls.

anya: Accessibility note: slider should have fine-grain steps (5% or 10ms) but keyboard + manual input allowed.

sam: Telemetry: emit metrics for "soft_swap_active" (boolean), "soft_swap_pct", "padding_ms", and an event when the swap crosses thresholds.

maria: Telemetry + audit should link to trace IDs so SRE can inspect examples. Add a "sample 10 example requests" action in the UI.

vik: Edge case: oscillation. If traffic fluctuates, we risk flip-flopping. Need hysteresis: once a swap engages, min hold time (configurable) before reverting. could be same as staging_padding or separate.

leon: Agreed — call it hold_seconds. default 60s. show it in the advanced section.

maria: UX copy for the advanced hover: "Hold time prevents rapid oscillation by keeping the fallback in effect for this period once triggered."

anya: One more: preview should show both "requests that would route to fallback" and "requests that would stay", plus an estimated cost delta per 1M requests. super helpful for ops.

maria: Implementation note for eng: we can simulate on a replay stream. but the console should warn when replay uses PII and ask for confirmation.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/fallback-ui -> staging at 2025-09-05T02:00:00Z.

sam: Quick API shape proposal for infra team: 
```json
{"policy_type":"soft_swap","padding_ms":300,"ramp_pct":20,"triggers":["5xx","oom"],"hold_seconds":60}
```

maria: Nice. ok lets capture action items: 1) design: slider + ramp + advanced hold + trigger selector + preview simulation (anya) 2) telemetry: metrics & event schema (sam) 3) infra: API contract + replay endpoint (vik) 4) security: PII confirmation in replay (leon).

leon: i'll draft the trigger dropdown options and copy for the tooltip.

anya: will mock the preview UI and chart tomorrow.

vik: i'll prototype audit breadcrumb fields.

maria: thanks all. quick sync after mocks. :thumbsup:
